- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is falling, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >60), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 64.72 → 59.12 → 58.33), model often fails to adjust — apply downward bias of 1–3% for 5–7 days post-spike.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently above true outcome by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to ignore sentiment — apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias if true outcome dips below 60.  
- If forecast is flat (±0.1) and true outcome shows volatility, adjust forecast to match volatility trend — e.g., if true drops 2% in 3 days, forecast should drop 1–1.5% per day.
